headline: PHP warned of a third unpatched code execution flaw while Mirai operators hammered the PHP2Shell bugs without a single confirmed compromise, and researchers found ransomware affiliates running whole intrusions through an autonomous AI framework.

emerging_trends.text: Criminals now hand intrusion work to software: affiliates of INC and The Gentlemen point an autonomous kill-chain framework called Phantom at victims, a separate tool hunts unprotected models to plan break-ins on the owner's bill, and Dark Reading clocked public models taking full domain control of a target for $12.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Ransomware Affiliates Run Autonomous AI Kill Chains

emerging_trends.text: Flaws keep landing in the parts nobody chooses—the Onigmo regular expression engine inside Ruby that produced four critical GitLab bugs, the Brotli decoder bundled into official Node.js images, and Pillow's handoff of file names to Ghostscript—so patching an application now means tracking what its dependencies decode.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Pillow and Node.js Decoders Run Attacker Code

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep skipping the exploit entirely: one campaign harvested more than 70,000 credentials off exposed Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks firewalls, another spent ten weeks on replayed sign-in sessions that need no password and no second factor, and Dark Reading found fraudsters calling help desks and politely asking for access.

topics.title: PHP2Shell Draws Mass Mirai Scanning
topics.latest_developments: PHP disclosed a third remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-115560, on October 23, 2026, two days after its emergency patches, and shipped no fix for it, telling administrators to turn off the feature involved because the bug reaches only web applications running an unusual configuration; the SANS Internet Storm Center returned its InfoCon gauge to green Friday morning and now doubts the original pair exploits reliably at all, Unit 42 updated its threat brief the same day, and researchers still confirm no successful compromise out of millions of attempts to enlist servers in the Mirai variant Potassium, even as exploit code that bypasses address space layout randomization circulates.
topics.summary: The pair of PHP flaws, each rated 9.2, give an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution on any PHP installation serving web requests, with the highest risk on Apache with mod_php and on PHP-FPM. Every site on PHP 8.2 through 8.5 needs the October 21, 2026 releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.

topics.title: Capcom and Quest Diagnostics Count Victims
topics.latest_developments: Capcom, the Japanese gaming company, confirmed that a third party reached CAPCOM ID, the account service people use to sign in to its web services and play some of its games online, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and changing the login passwords on 196 accounts; Capcom spotted suspicious activity on October 19, 2026 and confirmed the intrusion the same day, and Quest Diagnostics told securities regulators that an intruder reached Quanum Lab Services Manager, the platform certain clients use to place test orders, and touched certain patient records.
topics.summary: Capcom account holders should expect phishing mail that imitates the company and should rotate any password they reused elsewhere. Quest Diagnostics has yet to put a number on the patient records involved.

topics.title: Pillow and Node.js Decoders Run Attacker Code
topics.latest_developments: Ruby shipped versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13 on October 23, 2026 to fix three bugs in Onigmo, its built-in regular expression engine, which sit behind the four critical GitLab remote code execution flaws of the past month, because a crafted pattern corrupts memory while Ruby compiles it; researchers disclosed CVE-2026-112900 in Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, which passes an EPS file's name straight to Ghostscript and so runs whatever operating system command a caller buries in that name; Imperva published Node2Shell, a proof of concept that executed code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64 by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder, CVE-2026-111497; and Atlassian's October bulletin listed 176 vulnerability entries, 14 of them critical, all in third-party components of its Data Center and Server products.
topics.summary: Pillow decodes uploaded images across Python web applications, so any server that opens an attacker-named EPS file hands over a shell, and the Node.js proof of concept needed no debugger or custom build. Teams running Ruby, Pillow, Node.js, or Atlassian Data Center should install the current releases.

topics.title: Ransomware Affiliates Run Autonomous AI Kill Chains
topics.latest_developments: Researchers found exposed infrastructure belonging to affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups that reveals an AI-driven intrusion ecosystem built around Phantom, an autonomous red team kill chain framework run by a Russian-speaking operator who both breaks in and extorts; Dark Reading counted one campaign aiming open-weight models at 105 websites and another in which public models won full domain control of a target for $12; and SecurityWeek reported that China's Storm-0940 drove the agentic penetration-testing tool Artex through the ConnectWise compromise, reaching hundreds of organizations and privileged access in some environments.
topics.summary: Extortion crews and state groups alike now point agentic tools at reconnaissance, exploitation, and lateral movement, which collapses the time defenders get between first contact and encryption. Security teams should assume intrusion speed measured in hours and watch for machine-paced scanning and credential use inside their networks.

sources.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
AI Tools Are Generating Massive Attacks for Little Cost

topics.title: APT41 Bootkit and Sandworm's Mesh Backdoor
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky said the BlackX UEFI bootkit defeats Secure Boot on fully patched Windows machines whose owners never applied the certificate revocations for CVE-2022-21894, and named the victims as diplomatic organizations in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan hit in early 2026, with suspicion falling on the China-linked group APT41; ESET detailed the Ukrainian case, reporting that UAC-0099, also called Earth Sirrush, phished its way into a logistics company on July 16, 2025 and passed access to Sandworm, which installed a previously unseen mesh network backdoor before destroying data; and SecurityWeek reported that Iran's Prince of Persia group broke a three-month lull by hiding a Tornado command-and-control server on United States shared hosting, its first server in the country since 2016.
topics.summary: A bootkit that runs before Windows loads survives reinstallation and hides from every tool inside the operating system, and the Secure Boot fix requires loading the revocation list, a step many fleets skipped. Administrators should apply the CVE-2022-21894 revocations, and defenders tracking Iranian activity should stop treating domestic hosting as a trust signal.

topics.title: Third VeloCloud Orchestrator Zero-Day in Four Months
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek counted the actively exploited SQL injection flaw Arista Networks patched on October 22, 2026 as the third zero-day in VeloCloud Orchestrator in four months, a run that keeps handing attackers the management server for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks.
topics.summary: The critical flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even on a read-only customer account, reach privileged internal functionality and take operator privileges, the top level of control. Organizations running VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem should install Arista's updates and review orchestrator logins.

topics.title: Attackers Hijack Exposed AI Models and Agent Wallets
topics.latest_developments: Symantec researchers Priti More and Susmit Yenkar captured the instruction set of an attack tool that scans for AI models anyone on the internet can reach and then uses them to plan break-ins while the model's owner pays for the computing power, after its operators sent their entire working prompt to a honeypot posing as an unprotected AI service; the security firm V12 reported on October 22, 2026 that the default client in the x402 SDKs set no spending limit until the August 18 releases added one, so a malicious API could get an agent to sign a payment for its full balance of a supported token.
topics.summary: Both problems punish AI infrastructure left open by default: an unauthenticated model endpoint becomes an attacker's free hacking engine, and an agent that signs payments automatically becomes a wallet to empty. Operators should authenticate every model endpoint and set per-call spending caps on agent payment SDKs.

sources.title: Hackers hijack exposed AI models to launch cyberattacks at victims' expense
Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents' Token Balances

topics.title: Campaign Harvests 70,000 Credentials From Edge Firewalls
topics.latest_developments: Researchers disclosed on October 23, 2026 a large-scale campaign against internet-exposed network edge devices, among them Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect firewalls, that has exposed more than 70,000 credentials, and artifacts from the investigation show the operators already hold access at organizations worldwide and have pushed deeper into some of them.
topics.summary: The operators collect logins from the appliances that sit at the network perimeter, which hands them remote access that looks legitimate to everything behind it. Administrators should rotate firewall and VPN credentials, enforce multi-factor authentication on remote access, and hunt for unfamiliar sessions on edge devices.

sources.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials

topics.title: Microsoft 365 Session Replay Hits 79 Organizations
topics.latest_developments: Huntress reported on October 23, 2026 that one attacker spent ten weeks replaying stolen Microsoft 365 sign-in sessions against 79 organizations between July 14 and September 22, 2026, logging 497 successful sign-ins and more than 200,000 failed login attempts, planting hidden inbox rules that kept victims from seeing parts of their own mail, and running the replays from servers at the hosting provider 1337 Services GmbH.
topics.summary: A replayed session needs no password and no multi-factor code, so credential defenses miss it entirely. Security teams should revoke active sessions whenever they suspect a compromise, audit mailbox rules for hidden filters, and watch sign-ins from 1337 Services GmbH address space.

sources.title: Microsoft 365 accounts compromised at 79 organizations, no passwords needed

topics.summary: ArubaOS runs the controllers and gateways that carry enterprise Wi-Fi and branch networking, and an authentication bypass at that rating hands an unauthenticated attacker the device. Administrators should install the current ArubaOS builds and keep controller management interfaces off the public internet.

business_politics.summary: France's 10-year yield touched 5% this week for the first time since 2002 and its spread over German bunds sat at the widest since 2011, as riots over living costs and a fragmented parliament left Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's government short of a credible deficit plan. The affirmation lifts the immediate downgrade threat over Europe's most heavily traded sovereign credit six months before Emmanuel Macron's successor contest.

events.title: The Breakthrough T1D Walk Fills the North Shore
events.latest_developments: WPXI reported Friday, October 23, that thousands of people will gather on Pittsburgh's North Shore on Saturday, October 24, for the annual Breakthrough T1D Walk.
events.summary: The walk raises money for research toward a cure for type 1 diabetes and draws people living with the disease along with their friends and families.

sources.title: Breakthrough T1D hosting annual walk in Pittsburgh

events.title: Irwin Celebrates Halloween a Week Early
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Friday, October 23, that downtown Irwin holds its Halloween parade on Saturday, October 24, a week ahead of the holiday.
events.summary: The Westmoreland County borough pairs the parade with a storefront decorating contest and trick-or-treating at downtown businesses.

sources.title: Halloween parade, store trick-or-treat set for Irwin

events.title: Lee Terbosic Hangs Over Arts Landing
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Friday, October 23, that the magician Lee Terbosic will attempt a Houdini-style straitjacket escape high above Arts Landing on Halloween.
events.summary: Terbosic, a Pittsburgh native, once dangled upside down in a straitjacket from a wire 90 feet above downtown Pittsburgh, and he aims to top that stunt this time.

sources.title: Lee Terbosic to attempt Houdini-esque straitjacket escape from high above Arts Landing

events.title: A Pizza Musical Casts the Audience
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper previewed "Slice Something Slice" on Friday, October 23, an interactive musical about Pittsburgh pizza in which audience members take the starring role.
events.summary: The show grows out of the work of Dan Tallarico, the self-described pizza journalist who has reviewed Pittsburgh-area pizzerias through his blog Pizza Walk With Me, a Substack, and a newsletter, and who wrote a book on the subject; Tallarico argues the city punches above its weight on pizza.

sources.title: Bite into Slice Something Slice, a pizza musical where you're the star

around_teams.title: Benton and the Line Face the Media in Paris
around_teams.latest_developments: Keeanu Benton, Jamel Dean, Darnell Washington, and rookie defensive lineman Gabriel Rubio spoke with reporters from the Steelers' Paris hotel on Friday, October 23.
around_teams.summary: Benton and Rubio pick up the interior snaps the Steelers lost when they placed Sebastian Joseph-Day on injured reserve this week, two days before Pittsburgh meets the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France. Benton drew the team's best defensive-line grades for the Week 6 win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

sources.title: Benton, Dean, Washington & Rubio Press Conference (October 23) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Not Just Football Airs the Roberts Camp Interview
around_teams.latest_developments: Cam Heyward's show Not Just Football released a full training-camp interview with inside linebacker Elandon Roberts on Friday, October 23, holding it until Roberts re-signed with the Steelers.
around_teams.summary: Roberts walks through the single Steelers play he says changed his career. Heyward and co-host Hayden Walsh recorded the conversation during camp and shelved it when Roberts left the roster.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward
sources.title: The Steelers Play That Changed Elandon Roberts' Career

around_teams.title: Hiles Hunts an NFL Bar in Paris
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles published his search for a bar showing NFL football in Paris on Friday, October 23, as the team's channel posted its own Paris street videos.
around_teams.summary: Hiles walked the city looking for the places Steelers fans will fill before Sunday's 9:30 a.m. Eastern kickoff against the New Orleans Saints, the league's first regular-season game in France.

around_teams.title: The Steelers Set Up Shop in Paris
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers held their Friday, October 23, media sessions from their Paris hotel, with head coach Mike McCarthy, quarterback Aaron Rodgers, T.J. Watt, DK Metcalf, Pat Freiermuth, Cam Heyward, Patrick Queen, and Jaylen Warren all speaking, and the Post-Gazette reported the players see the trip as a chance to showcase NFL football and themselves.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh meets the New Orleans Saints at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on Sunday, October 25, at the Stade de France, the league's first regular-season game in the country. Former Steelers Santonio Holmes and Ryan Shazier joined the team's channel live from Paris, where the club has sequestered itself in a hotel in the center of the city.

around_teams.title: Elliott Could Play a Year After His Injury
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday morning, October 23, that Steelers safety DeShon Elliott could return Sunday against the New Orleans Saints in Paris, a year removed from the injury the paper calls gruesome.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers ruled Elliott out of the October 18 game at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and his return would hand defensive coordinator Patrick Graham a starting safety back for the 9:30 a.m. Eastern kickoff Sunday, October 25, in a secondary already missing pieces.

sources.title: Steelers safety DeShon Elliott could return Sunday, a year removed from his gruesome injury

around_teams.title: Rodgers Would Back 16 Games Abroad in a Week
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, October 23, that quarterback Aaron Rodgers said the NFL could stage 16 international games in a single week and that he would support the idea.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers made the case as the Steelers prepared to meet the New Orleans Saints in Paris on Sunday, October 25, the league's first regular-season game in France, one of the international dates the NFL keeps adding to the schedule.

sources.title: Aaron Rodgers says the NFL could play 16 international games in one week — and he'd support it

around_teams.title: The Steelers Fly Out for Paris
around_teams.latest_developments: The team's channel posted its departure videos, "Next stop: Paris" and "Bon voyage," early Friday, October 23, as the Steelers left for France, alongside a clip of Hall of Famers Dermontti Dawson and Mel Blount checking in from Paris on Thursday, October 22.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh meets the New Orleans Saints at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on Sunday, October 25, on NFL Network, and the team has filled the week with throwback highlights of running back Willie Parker and tight end Heath Miller against the Saints; defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day stays home on injured reserve, with two rookie defensive linemen taking his snaps.

team_usa.title: Skye Blakely Wins the World All-Around Title
team_usa.latest_developments: Skye Blakely won the women's all-around gold at the world gymnastics championships on Friday, October 23, in the Netherlands, a result she called a dream.
team_usa.summary: Blakely's title restores an American name at the top of the sport two days after China edged the United States for the team gold and ended a long run of American dominance, and she did it with the Olympic champion Hezly Rivera out of the meet with an ankle injury.

sources.title: U.S.'s Blakely captures 'dream' all-around gold at gymnastics worlds

team_usa.title: USA Hockey Extends Wroblewski Through 2030
team_usa.latest_developments: USA Hockey extended John Wroblewski's contract as head coach of the United States women's national team through the 2030 Olympics, ESPN reported Friday, October 23.
team_usa.summary: Wroblewski coached the Americans to the gold medal at the Milan Cortina Games in February, and the extension keeps him through the next Winter Olympic cycle.

sources.title: USA Hockey extends women's coach Wroblewski through '30 Olympics

team_usa.title: Scally Scores to Spare Gladbach a Record
team_usa.latest_developments: United States defender Joe Scally scored in Borussia Mönchengladbach's 3-2 win at Stuttgart on Friday, October 23.
team_usa.summary: The result kept Gladbach from becoming the first club in Bundesliga history to lose its first seven games of a season, and it strengthens Scally's case for a place in head coach Mauricio Pochettino's squad before the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti in November.

sources.title: USMNT's Scally scores, helps Gladbach avoid worst-ever Bundesliga start

team_usa.title: Musah Plays His Way Back Into the USMNT Picture
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Friday, October 23, that Yunus Musah has reclaimed a midfield role at AC Milan and put himself back in contention for the United States men's national team.
team_usa.summary: Musah spent last season on loan at Atalanta, where he played little and rarely in the middle of the field. Back at Milan in his preferred position, he gives head coach Mauricio Pochettino's squad another central option before the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti in November.

sources.title: Musah is back in Milan, back in midfield and back in contention for the USMNT
